summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old woman with alcoholic cirrhosis and a history of chronic abdominal pain was admitted due to worsening epigastric and left lower quadrant pain and acute kidney injury. She had poor oral intake for two days, leading to prerenal azotemia with creatinine rising from a baseline of 1.0 to 1.5, peaking at 1.8, then improving to 1.1 with IV fluids and albumin. Imaging showed cirrhosis without ascites and no evidence of ileus. Urinalysis showed pyuria, but culture revealed fecal contamination, ruling out infection. Pain was attributed to chronic abdominal issues possibly exacerbated by constipation and motility dysfunction. She remained stable without evidence of GI bleeding or hepatic decompensation. She was discharged home with improved renal function, pain control on oral medications, and recommendations to follow up with gastroenterology for motility evaluation and to complete outpatient lab testing.
